from System Review to a GaN Building Block
Enes Ayaz, Shahriar Sarmast Ghahfarokhi, Kevin Klarin, Staffan Norrga
Division of Electric Power and Energy Systems, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden
A · Review: what the SPB architecture demands
Concept: split the dc voltage, keep one machine
N-cell SPB: series dc links, separate winding groups
Integration concept: cold plate, legs, busbar
N two-level bridges in series on
the dc side; each feeds its own
All cells carry the same dc
the system, it does not vanish.
Device voltage class and cell count
1200 V link: Vcell = Vdc/N versus active switches 6N
Lower blocking voltage raises the device figure of merit
Rating with margin: Vrated ≥ krel(Vdc,max/N + ΔVimb + ΔVsw).
N = 16 gives 75 V cells for 100 V GaN; the overshoot L·di/dt
Shared dc current of three cells, with and without interleaving
Carrier interleaving δk = 2π(k−1)/N cancels carrier orders that
Cell k sits at the offset (k−1)Vdc/N: a stack-position
Complementary two-cell switching cancels the switching CMV only
Differential power ΔPk restores equal cell voltages (motoring)
The open-loop series stack is unstable in motoring: N−1
Centralized, common-duty-ratio and distributed control trade
A faulted cell must be bypassed without breaking the series dc
B · Design flow and the four-parallel GaN building block
Constraints → device, layout, parallel count, dc link, machine → coupled verification
This project: EPC2361, N = 16, np = 4 per switch, 50 kHz, 134 µF effective per
leg; Q3D-extracted loops feed the LTspice double-pulse model.
Building block: final double-pulse-test board (Rev B)
DPT board: four cells, M6 ac bolt and copper bar
Eight EPC2361 from above (heatsink, shunts hidden)
89.5 × 85.2 mm, 4 layers, 2 oz, 0.1 mm L1–L2 dielectric: every
loop closes vertically on the dc− plane.
Four cells in two point-symmetric blocks; one 2EDF7275K per
Per cell 20 × 22 µF 2220 + 10 × 1 µF; Rg,on 3.5 Ω, −1.9 V
1 mΩ coaxial shunt per cell; MMCX and spring-probe pads for
vDS, vGS of all eight devices.
LTspice with the extracted network (75 V, 322 A)
High-side vDS peak 92.9 V < 100 V rating
Four parallel high-side gate loops equal within 0.3 %
DPT board released for JLCPCB PCB + assembly; shunts and loop
test points fitted in the lab.
Double-pulse tests at 75 V up to 322 A: per-cell current sharing,
Then three load-test legs + PCB busbar: one 75 V three-phase
Optimum N: device class versus component count shifts with SiC,
Joint battery–converter–machine design on vehicle energy, mass,
Stack-position CMV, bearing currents and insulation across the
SPB moves the voltage problem from the device to the system: the building block shows that a 100 V GaN cell meets its loop and overshoot budget;
the review sets out what the full stack must still prove — balancing, common mode, faults and machine co-design.
